# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P8_08",

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1 Introduction and functional overview\nTime Synchronization between different applications and/or ECUs is of paramount im-\nportance when correlation of different events across a distributed system is needed,\neither to be able to track such events in time or to trigger them at an accurate point in\ntime.\nFor this reason, a Time Synchronization API is offered to the Application, so it can\nretrieve the time information synchronized with other entities / ECUs.\nFor the format, message sequences and semantics of the time synchronization pro-\ntocols to use, please refer to the Protocol Requirements Specicification (PRS) of the\nAUTOSAR Time synchronization Protocol (see [1]).\nThe Time Synchronization functionality is then offered by means of different \"Time\nBase Resources\" (from now on referred to as TBR).\nThese TBRs are classified in different types. These types have an equivalent design\nto the types of the time bases offered in the Synchronized Time Base Manager speci-\nfication [2] (from now on referred to as StbM). The classification is the following:\n•\nSynchronized Master Time Base\n•\nOffset Master Time Base\n•\nSynchronized Slave Time Base\n•\nOffset Slave Time Base\nAs in StbM, the TBRs offered by the Time Synchronization module (TS from now on),\nare also synchronized with other Time Bases on other nodes of a distributed system.\nThe Application consumes the time information provided and managed by the TBRs.\nTherefore, the TBRs serve as Time Base brokers, offering access to Synchronized\nTime Bases. By doing so, the TS module abstracts from the \"real\" Time Base provider.\n8 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n3 Related documentation\n3.1 Input documents & related standards and norms\n[1] Time Synchronization Protocol Specification\nAUTOSAR_FO_PRS_TimeSyncProtocol\n[2] Specification of Synchronized Time-Base Manager\nAUTOSAR_CP_SWS_SynchronizedTimeBaseManager\n[3] Glossary\nAUTOSAR_FO_TR_Glossary\n[4] Requirements on Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR_FO_RS_TimeSync\n[5] General Requirements specific to Adaptive Platform\nAUTOSAR_AP_RS_General\n[6] Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core\n[7] Explanation of Adaptive Platform Software Architecture\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture\n[8] ISO/IEC 14882:2011, Information technology  Programming languages  C++\nhttps://www.iso.org\n[9] Standard for Information TechnologyPortable Operating System Interface\n(POSIX(R)) Base Specifications, Issue 7\nhttp://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/\n[10] Specification of Time Synchronization over Ethernet\nAUTOSAR_CP_SWS_TimeSyncOverEthernet\n[11] Specification of Manifest\nAUTOSAR_AP_TPS_ManifestSpecification\nNOTE: [5, RS-RSGeneral] is listed here as an input document because it applies to\nSWS TimeSync as well as to all SWS documents of the Adaptive Platform. Since it\nincludes only non-functional requirements the tracing is not necessary.\n3.2 Further applicable specification\nAUTOSAR provides a core specification [6, SWS AdaptiveCore] which is also appli-\ncable for\nTime Synchronization\n. The chapter \"General requirements for all Func-\ntional Clusters\" of this specification shall be considered as an additional and required\nspecification for implementation of\nTime Synchronization\n.\n11 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"

      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Known limitations\nThe Time Synchronization module is bound to Adaptive Platform Systems.\n4.1.1 Configuration\nPlease refer to the corresponding model elements.\n4.1.2 Time Gateway\nTime Gateway functionality is currently not in scope of the Time Synchronization mod-\nule for the Adaptive Platform.\n4.1.3 Out of Scope\nErrors, which occurred during Global Time establishment and which are not caused by\nthe module itself (i.e. loss of PTP global time is not an issue of the TS but of the TSP\nmodules) are out of the scope of this module.\n4.1.4 Security\nSecured Time Synchronization using the AUTOSAR Sub-TLV: Time Authenticated (see\nPRS-TimeSync [1]) is currently not supported for the Adaptive Platform.\nNote:\nSecured Time Synchronization messages received in AP ECUs works with-\nout verifying the security measures (i.e., AUTOSAR Sub-TLV:Time Authenticated is\nignored).\n4.1.5 Offset Time Bases\nThe Time Synchronization module of the Adaptive Platform does not support rate cor-\nrection for Offset Time Bases.\n12 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P13_15",

      "source_page": 13,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4.2 Applicability to car domains\nThe concept is targeted at supporting time-critical automotive applications. This does\nnot mean that the concept has all that is required by such systems though, but crucial\ntiming-related features which cannot be deferred to implementation are considered.\n4.3 Recommendation\nIn the case where the TSP is based on Ethernet, the protocol to be used is defined in\nthe PRS (see [1]).\n...\n13 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7 Functional specification\nThe functional behavior is described under the following specific contexts:\n•\nStartup Behavior\n•\nShutdown Behavior\n•\nConstruction Behavior (Initialization)\n•\nNormal Operation\n•\nError Handling\n•\nError Classification\n•\nVersion Check\n7.1 General Overview of TS\nFor the Adaptive Platform, three different technologies were considered to fulfill such\nTime Synchronization requirements. These technologies were:\n•\nStbM of the Classic Platform\n•\nLibrary chrono - either std::chrono (C++11) or boost::chrono [8]\n•\nThe Time posix interface [9]\nThe following table shows the interfaces provided to the Application by means of this\nAPI and their equivalent interface in StbM."

      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Table 7.1: Interface comparison between TS and STBM\n7.1.1 Base functionality of every Time Base\nEvery Time Base has to provide a minimum set of functionality, as listed below:\n•\noffer possibility to obtain the current timestamp\n•\ncreating a snapshot of its parameters\nThis chapter briefly describes these functionalities. Details on how to use and the exact\nbehavior of these core methods are given in chapter 8.\n7.1.1.1 Time Base Status\nThis\nTimeBaseStatus\nis a snapshot of all the information of a Time Base Resource\nit is related to, like status flags, amount of times the TBR has been updated, time\nleap information (possibly generated during the last synchronization of the Time Base\nResource), etc.\n7.1.1.2 Rate Deviation\nApplications will have different thresholds for acceptable time drift values. Hence there\nneeds to be a way, how applications can access this information.\n[SWS_TS_00202]\n⌈\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::Ge-\ntRateDeviation\nshall return the calculated rate deviation of its TBR against the\ntime source it is synchronized to. In case there is no rate deviation calculated yet, the\ninitial rate deviation of 0.0 shall be returned.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\nNote:\nFor more information of how rate deviation is calculated see: 7.3.6 Time Correc-\ntion.\n7.1.1.3 Clock Time Value\nReading the clock's time value is very likely the most commonly performed operation\nby the applications interacting with TS.\n22 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"

      "source_page": 23,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nTo ensure type safe handling of time values, the timepoint is provided as std::chrono\nstructure.\nMore detailed information on how this is implemented is given in the further chapters\nand in chapter 8.\n7.1.2 Status Flags of TBRs\nTime Synchronization defines a set of status flags that are used to express specific\nstatus conditions of a TBR. Status flags can be queried by an application through a\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetTimeWithStatus\n.\nSynchronization status GetSynchronizationStatus includes:\n•\nkNotSynchronizedUntilStartup\n: Indicates whether a synchronization of a\ntime base to its corresponding TBR happend until start-up (initial state)\n•\nkTimeOut\n: Indicates whether a synchronization of a time base to its correspond-\ning TBR is lost or delayed.\n•\nkSynchronized\n: Indicates if the time base of the corresponding TBR has been\nsuccessfully synchronized at least once against its time source.\n•\nkSynchToGateway\n: Indicates if the corresponding TBR updates are based on\na Time Gateway below the Global Time Master.\nThe status if a leap jump happend since the last status request through a GetTime-\nWithStatus could be retrieved via GetLeapJump:\n•\nkTimeLeapNone\n: Indicates that no leap jump happend\n•\nkTimeLeapFuture\n: Indicates if there has been a jump in time to the future.\n•\nkTimeLeapPast\n: Indicates if there has been a jump in time to the past.\n7.1.3 Time Synchronization and Protocols\nTime Synchronization mechanisms and protocols (i.e. [10] are out of the Scope of this\ndocument, for protocol specification please refer to the PRS (see [1]).\n7.2 Functional cluster life cycle\n7.2.1 Startup\nThis chapter describes the necessary initializations, which are performed by the entity\nthat has control over the Time Base Resources, in order to prepare the TS module for\n23 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"

Then the value of the '\nTimeBaseProviderToPersistencyMap-\nping\n.\ncyclicBackupInterval\n' itself shall be added and this check-pointed value\nof the Global Time shall then be stored into persistent memory '\nTimeBaseProvider-\nToPersistencyMapping\n.\ntimeBaseProvider\n' (see [11]) as\nbackupTimestamp\nif\npersistent storage is required. The initial value of\nbackupTimestamp\nshall be set to\n0\n.\nUpon a graceful shutdown the Global Time shall be stored without applying\nanother '\nTimeBaseProviderToPersistencyMapping\n.\ncyclicBackupInterval\n'\nas back-off.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00024)\nNote:\nRegardless of the exact shutdown event, the last stored value of\nbackupTi-\nmestamp\nwill be restored during the next startup (see 7.2.1).\n7.3 Normal Operation\n7.3.1 Introduction\nA Global Time network consists of a Time Master and at least one Time Slave. The Time Slave corrects the\nreceived Global Time Base taking into account the Time Stamp at the transmitter side\nand the own generated receiver Time Stamp.\nThe local time of a Slave Time Base will be maintained autonomously and updated\nwhenever a new time value is received from its associated Master Time Base.\n25 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.3.2.2 Time Slave\nIn the role of a Time Slave, the TBR updates its internally-maintained local time to a\nvalue of a Global Time Base, which is provided by the corresponding TSP module.\n7.3.3 Time Base Resources\n7.3.3.1 Slave Time Bases\n[SWS_TS_00139]\n⌈\nMonitoring of time leaps to the future shall only be value of\nara::tsync::LeapJump\nshall be\nkTime-\nLeapNone\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n[SWS_TS_00028]\n⌈\nActive Time Leap Status\nara::tsync::LeapJump\nshall be set to\nkTimeLeapNone\n, if a consecutive       "source_page": 28,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_TS_00033]\n⌈\nIf the update of the Time Base is successful and the\nSYNC_TO_GATEWAY bit is NOT set, the\nara::tsync::SynchronizationSta-\ntus\nshall be set to\nkSynchronized\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n7.3.4 Immediate Time Synchronization\nAll TSP Modules are working independently of the TS regarding the handling of the\nbus-specific Time Synchronization protocol (i.e. autonomous transmission of Timesync\nmessages on the bus).\nTime information is passed from a TSP to the TBR. Implementation details as well as\nthe interaction of such a TSP with the TBR are outside of the scope of this specifica-\ntion(for protocol specification please refer to [1]).\n7.3.5 User Data\nUser Data is part of each Time Base. User Data is set by the Global Time Master of\neach Time Base and distributed as part of the Timesync messages.\nUser Data can be used to characterize the Time Base, e.g., regarding the quality of the\nunderlying clock source or regarding the progress of time.\nUser Data consists of a vector of bytes. Due to the frame format of various Timesync\nmessages it might not be possible to transmit the complete vector on every bus system.\nIt is the responsibility of the system designer to use only those User Data bytes in the\nvector that can be distributed inside the vehicle network.\n7.3.6 Time Correction\nTS provides the ability for Time Slaves to perform Rate and Offset Correction of the\nSynchronized TBR and Rate Correction of an Offset Time Base.\nFor Global Time Masters, the TS provides the ability to perform Rate Correction of their\nTime Base(s).\nTime correction can be configured individually for each Time Base.\n7.3.6.1 Rate Correction for Time Slaves\nRate Correction detects and eliminates rate deviations of local instances of Time Bases\nand of Offset Time Bases. Rate Correction determines the rate deviation in the scope\nof a measurement. This rate deviation is used as correction factor which the TBR\nuses to correct the Time Base's time whenever it is read (e.g. in the scope of\nara::\ntsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetCurrentTime\n).\n28 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_TS_00701]\n⌈\nA registered notifier via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTime-\nBaseConsumer::RegisterStatusChangeNotifier\nshall be invoked, if one of\nthe following content is changed:\nara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus\n,\nara::\ntsync::LeapJump\nor the\nuser data\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00021)\n7.3.7.2 Synchronization status notification\nA change in the StatusFlags of the\nara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus\n(e.g.\nif the timebase is in Timeout) can be notified.\n[SWS_TS_00702]\n⌈\nA registered notifier via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTime-\nBaseConsumer::RegisterSynchronizationStateChangeNotifier\nshall be\ninvoked, if\nara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus\nis changed.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n7.3.7.3 LeapJump notification\nA leap jump can be notified.\n[SWS_TS_00703]\n⌈\nA registered notifier via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTime-\nBaseConsumer::RegisterTimeLeapNotifier\nshall be invoked, if\nara::\ntsync::LeapJump\nis changed.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n7.3.8 Global Time Precision Measurement Support\nTo verify the precision of each Local Time Base compared to the Global Time Base\na recording mechanism shall be optionally supported for Time Slaves and Time Gate-\nways. In principle, a snapshot is taken of all required data at the point in time, where\na synchronization event takes place. Access is provided to those values by an actively\npushed API function on each successful assembled data block. An Off-Board Tester\ncollects each block and calculates the precision afterwards and maintains a history of\nrecorded blocks and their elements accordingly. How and by which protocol the data\nwill be transferred to the Off-Board Tester will be specified by the Application.\n[SWS_TS_00803]\n⌈\nA registration via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseCon-\nsumer::RegisterTimePrecisionMeasurementNotifier\nshall only be possible\nfor Synchronized Time Bases and Offset Time Bases, for which\nisSystemWideGlob-\nalTimeMaster\nis set to FALSE.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n[SWS_TS_00800]\n⌈\nFor Synchronized Time Bases, a registered TimePrecisionMea-\nsurement notifier (via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::Reg-\nisterTimePrecisionMeasurementNotifier\n) shall write the block elements\n•\nglbSeconds\n•\nglbNanoSeconds\n33 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"

GlbSeconds, Glb-\nNanoSeconds are the elements of the Global Time part of the Received Time Tuple\n(i.e., TGRx); VirtualLocalTimeLow is the nanosecondsLo element of the Virtual Local\nTime part of the Received Time Tuple (i.e., TVRx).\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n[SWS_TS_00801]\n⌈\nFor Offset Time Bases, a registered TimePrecisionMeasure-\nment notifier (via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::Regis-\nterTimePrecisionMeasurementNotifier\n) shall only write the block elements\nGlbSeconds, GlbNanoSeconds and TimeBaseStatus to the related measurement\nrecording table.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n7.3.9 Global Time Validation Measurement Support\nFigure 7.3 outlines the basic concept of the Time Validation feature.\nA Time Slave collects information on the time synchronization process, to predict e.g.\nthe Sync Ingress based on its local instance of Global Time and check whether Master\nand Slave agree upon the current time. The prediction itself will be locally analyzed\nby a separate Adaptive Application to detect any existing impairments. Furthermore,\ninformation on the time synchronization process from Time Masters and Slaves is also\nshared with a Validator Adaptive Application which may run anywhere in the network,\ne.g. on the owner of Global Time.\nThe Validator uses the information on the time synchronization process received from\nthe Time Master and Time Slave Entities via a user defined feedback channel to re-\nconstruct the whole synchronization process and check that a coherent time base is\nestablished among all peers.\nThe Time Validation feature only provides API to the Adaptive Application. The feed-\nback channel and the actual validation performed by the respective Adaptive Applica-\ntion is not standardized in AUTOSAR. It is done in a user defined way on application\nlevel.\n34 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"

      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.3: Time Validation mechanism\nFor an optional validation of the Timesync and Pdelay mechanisms, the Time Synchro-\nnization functional cluster provides the following functionality.\n[SWS_TS_00424]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nEverytime a\nFollow_Up\nmessage is received, all pa-\nrameters defined by\nara::tsync::TimeSlaveMeasurementType\nshall be up-\ndated and the function\nara::tsync::ConsumerTimeBaseValidationNotifi-\ncation::SetSlaveTimingData\nshall be invoked.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n[SWS_TS_00425]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nEverytime a Sync message is transmitted, all pa-\nrameters defined by\nara::tsync::TimeMasterMeasurementType\nshall be up-\ndated and the function\nara::tsync::ProviderTimeBaseValidationNotifi-\ncation::SetMasterTimingData\nshall be invoked.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n[SWS_TS_00426]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nAfter the current Pdelay measurement is finished,\ni.e., upon reception of the\nPdelay_Resp_Follow_Up\nmessage, all parame-\nters defined by\nara::tsync::PdelayInitiatorMeasurementType\nshall be up-\ndated and the function\nara::tsync::ConsumerTimeBaseValidationNotifi-\ncation::SetPdelayInitiatorData\nshall be invoked.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n[SWS_TS_00427]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nAfter the current\nPdelay\nmeasurement is finished, i.e.,\nupon transmission of the\nPdelay_Resp_Follow_Up\n, all parameters defined by\nara::tsync::PdelayResponderMeasurementType\nshall be updated and the\nfunction\nara::tsync::ProviderTimeBaseValidationNotification::Set-\nPdelayResponderData\nshall be invoked.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n35 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nB Interfaces to other Functional Clusters (informative)\nNote:\nThis is chapter is created in the scope of the new SWS document template and\nin the current version is not applicable.\nB.1 Overview\nAUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between\nFunctional Clusters (on platform-level only), to allow efficient implementations, which\nmight depend e.g. on the used Operating System.\nThis chapter provides informative guidelines how the interaction between Functional\nClusters looks like, by clustering the relevant requirements of this document to describe\nInter-Functional Cluster (IFC) interfaces.   "bisheriges_fragment": "<div class=\"ai module-guide\">\n<p class=\"ai-note\">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p>\n\n<h3>Rolle & Verwendungszweck</h3>\n<p>Time Synchronization (<code>ara::tsync</code>) stellt der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform hochpräzise, netzwerkweit synchronisierte Zeitbasen bereit. In modernen Fahrzeugarchitekturen ist eine konsistente Zeitreferenz über mehrere Steuergeräte hinweg unerlässlich — insbesondere für Sensorfusion, bild- und radargestützte Fahrerassistenzsysteme (ADAS), deterministische Ereignisprotokollierung sowie echtzeitkritische Regelungen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00001\">[SWS_TS_00001]</a>.</p>\n<p>Das Modul realisiert die Anbindung an standardisierte Zeitsynchronisationsprotokolle wie gPTP (IEEE 802.1AS / IEEE 1588) über Ethernet sowie busspezifische Zeitsynchronisationsmechanismen (z. B. CAN-TSyn). Es unterscheidet funktional zwischen Time Master (Knoten, die als globale Zeitquelle fungieren oder Zeitinformationen weiterverteilen) und Time Slave (Knoten, die externe Zeitbotschaften empfangen, Pfadverzögerungen kompensieren und die lokale Uhr disziplinieren) <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00010\">[SWS_TS_00010]</a>.</p>\n\n<h3>Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge</h3>\n<p>Die C++-Schnittstellen von <code>ara::tsync</code> orientieren sich eng an den Standards von <code>std::chrono</code> und bieten darüber hinaus spezialisierte Verträge für automobilrelevante Zeitstatusprüfungen:</p>\n<ul>\n  <li><strong>SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer:</strong> Zentraler API-Einstiegspunkt für Anwendungen, die eine synchronisierte Zeitbasis konsumieren <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01001\">[SWS_TS_01001]</a>. Über <code>GetCurrentTime()</code> wird ein synchronisierter Zeitstempel als <code>ara::core::Result<TimePoint></code> abgerufen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01007\">[SWS_TS_01007]</a>.</li>\n  <li><strong>Ratenabweichung und Zeitstatus:</strong> Mit <code>GetRateDeviation()</code> lässt sich die aktuelle Frequenz- bzw. Ratenabweichung der Uhr (Drift) ermitteln <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01008\">[SWS_TS_01008]</a>. Die Methode <code>GetTimeWithStatus()</code> liefert den Zeitwert atomar zusammen mit dem aktuellen Gültigkeits- und Synchronisationszustand <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01009\">[SWS_TS_01009]</a>.</li>\n  <li><strong>Ereignis- und Statussignalisierung:</strong> Anwendungen können Callback-Handler für Statuswechsel (<code>RegisterStatusChangeNotifier()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01010\">[SWS_TS_01010]</a>), Änderungen des Synchronisationszustands (<code>RegisterSynchronizationStateChangeNotifier()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01012\">[SWS_TS_01012]</a>) sowie Zeitspünge (<code>RegisterTimeLeapNotifier()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01014\">[SWS_TS_01014]</a>) registrieren. Zur Überwachung der Einhaltung vorgegebener Präzisionskorridore dient <code>RegisterTimePrecisionMeasurementNotifier()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01018\">[SWS_TS_01018]</a>.</li>\n  <li><strong>Statusobjekt SynchronizedTimeBaseStatus:</strong> Kapselt Metadaten zum Synchronisationszustand, darunter Erstellungszeitpunkt (<code>GetCreationTime()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01055\">[SWS_TS_01055]</a>), Synchronisationsstatus (<code>GetSynchronizationStatus()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01053\">[SWS_TS_01053]</a>), erkannte Zeitsprünge (<code>GetLeapJump()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01054\">[SWS_TS_01054]</a>) sowie anwendungsspezifische Benutzerdaten (<code>GetUserData()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01056\">[SWS_TS_01056]</a>).</li>\n  <li><strong>SynchronizedTimeBaseProvider:</strong> Dient Subsystemen, die selbst als lokale oder externe Zeitquelle agieren, zur Bereitstellung und periodischen Einspeisung der Zeitbasis samt Zeitvalidierungsnotifikationen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01114\">[SWS_TS_01114]</a>.</li>\n</ul>\n\n<h3>Interaktionsfluss</h3>\n<p>Im laufenden Betrieb synchronisiert der Hintergrunddienst von <code>ara::tsync</code> die lokale Uhr kontinuierlich anhand eingehender Protokollbotschaften (z. B. PTP-Sync- und Follow-Up-Frames). Sobald die Zeitabweichung unter den konfigurierten Schwellwert sinkt, meldet das System den Zustand <code>kSynchronized</code> über registrierte Notifier. §11.2.2.2.1.1 „Get Value Of Time Base"</a>.</p><h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>
<p><code>SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetTimeWithStatus()</code> liefert eine Momentaufnahme aus globaler und lokaler Zeit, Synchronisationsstatus, Leap-Status und Nutzdaten. <code>kNotSynchronizedUntilStartup</code> kennzeichnet den Initialzustand, <code>kTimeOut</code> eine verlorene oder verzögerte Synchronisation; erfolgreiche Updates setzen <code>kSynchronized</code> beziehungsweise <code>kSynchToGateway</code>. Jede Consumer-Instanz überwacht den Zeitraum seit dem letzten Update gegen <code>syncLossTimeout</code> und setzt bei Ablauf <code>kTimeOut</code>. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS Time Synchronization §7.1.2 „Status Flags of TBRs“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_14218">[SWS_TS_14218]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00030">[SWS_TS_00030]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00032">[SWS_TS_00032]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00011">[SWS_TS_00011]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00033">[SWS_TS_00033]</a></p>
<p>Die Leap-Überwachung ist erst nach einer ersten Synchronisation und nur bei einem von null verschiedenen Schwellwert aktiv. Überschreitet die Resynchronisationsanpassung den jeweiligen Schwellwert, wird <code>LeapJump</code> auf <code>kTimeLeapFuture</code> oder <code>kTimeLeapPast</code> gesetzt; Änderungen des Synchronisations- und Leap-Status können über die vorgesehenen Notifier beobachtet werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.2.3.1">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2.3.1 „Slave Time Bases“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00139">[SWS_TS_00139]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00140">[SWS_TS_00140]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00141">[SWS_TS_00141]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00027">[SWS_TS_00027]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.2.7.2">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2.7.2 „Synchronization status notification“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00702">[SWS_TS_00702]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.2.7.3">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2.7.3 „LeapJump notification“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00703">[SWS_TS_00703]</a></p>

Zeit, Synchronisationsstatus, Leap-Status und Nutzdaten. <code>kNotSynchronizedUntilStartup</code> kennzeichnet den Initialzustand, <code>kTimeOut</code> eine verlorene oder verzögerte Synchronisation; erfolgreiche Updates setzen <code>kSynchronized</code> beziehungsweise <code>kSynchToGateway</code>. Jede Consumer-Instanz überwacht den Zeitraum seit dem letzten Update gegen <code>syncLossTimeout</code> und setzt bei Ablauf <code>kTimeOut</code>. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS Time Synchronization §7.1.2 „Status Flags of TBRs“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_14218">[SWS_TS_14218]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00030">[SWS_TS_00030]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00032">[SWS_TS_00032]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00011">[SWS_TS_00011]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00033">[SWS_TS_00033]</a></p> <p>Die Leap-Überwachung ist erst nach einer ersten Synchronisation und nur bei einem von null verschiedenen Schwellwert aktiv. Specification of Time Synchronization
AUTOSAR AP R23-11
1 Introduction and functional overview
Time Synchronization between different applications and/or ECUs is of paramount im-
portance when correlation of different events across a distributed system is needed,
either to be able to track such events in time or to trigger them at an accurate point in
time.
For this reason, a Time Synchronization API is offered to the Application, so it can
retrieve the time information synchronized with other entities / ECUs.
For the format, message sequences and semantics of the time synchronization pro-
tocols to use, please refer to the Protocol Requirements Specicification (PRS) of the
AUTOSAR Time synchronization Protocol (see [1]).
The Time Synchronization functionality is then offered by means of different "Time
Base Resources" (from now on referred to as TBR).
These TBRs are classified in different types. These types have an equivalent design
to the types of the time bases offered in the Synchronized Time Base Manager speci-
fication [2] (from now on referred to as StbM). The classification is the following:
•
Synchronized Master Time Base
•
Offset Master Time Base
•
Synchronized Slave Time Base
•
Offset Slave Time Base
As in StbM, the TBRs offered by the Time Synchronization module (TS from now on),
are also synchronized with other Time Bases on other nodes of a distributed system.
The Application consumes the time information provided and managed by the TBRs.
Therefore, the TBRs serve as Time Base brokers, offering access to Synchronized
Time Bases. By doing so, the TS module abstracts from the "real" Time Base provider.

4 Constraints and assumptions
4.1 Known limitations
The Time Synchronization module is bound to Adaptive Platform Systems.
4.1.1 Configuration
Please refer to the corresponding model elements.
4.1.2 Time Gateway
Time Gateway functionality is currently not in scope of the Time Synchronization mod-
ule for the Adaptive Platform.
4.1.3 Out of Scope
Errors, which occurred during Global Time establishment and which are not caused by
the module itself (i.e. loss of PTP global time is not an issue of the TS but of the TSP
modules) are out of the scope of this module.
4.1.4 Security
Secured Time Synchronization using the AUTOSAR Sub-TLV: Time Authenticated (see
PRS-TimeSync [1]) is currently not supported for the Adaptive Platform.
Note:
Secured Time Synchronization messages received in AP ECUs works with-
out verifying the security measures (i.e., AUTOSAR Sub-TLV:Time Authenticated is
ignored).
4.1.5 Offset Time Bases
The Time Synchronization module of the Adaptive Platform does not support rate cor-
rection for Offset Time Bases.

7.1.2 Status Flags of TBRs
Time Synchronization defines a set of status flags that are used to express specific
status conditions of a TBR. Status flags can be queried by an application through a
ara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetTimeWithStatus
.
Synchronization status GetSynchronizationStatus includes:
•
kNotSynchronizedUntilStartup
: Indicates whether a synchronization of a
time base to its corresponding TBR happend until start-up (initial state)
•
kTimeOut
: Indicates whether a synchronization of a time base to its correspond-
ing TBR is lost or delayed.
•
kSynchronized
: Indicates if the time base of the corresponding TBR has been
successfully synchronized at least once against its time source.
•
kSynchToGateway
: Indicates if the corresponding TBR updates are based on
a Time Gateway below the Global Time Master.
The status if a leap jump happend since the last status request through a GetTime-
WithStatus could be retrieved via GetLeapJump:
•
kTimeLeapNone
: Indicates that no leap jump happend
•
kTimeLeapFuture
: Indicates if there has been a jump in time to the future.
•
kTimeLeapPast
: Indicates if there has been a jump in time to the past.

7.3 Normal Operation
7.3.1 Introduction
A Global Time network consists of a Time Master and at least one Time Slave. For
each Time Domain, the Time Master is distributing the Global Time Base to the con-
nected Time Slaves via Time Synchronization messages. The Time Slave corrects the
received Global Time Base taking into account the Time Stamp at the transmitter side
and the own generated receiver Time Stamp.
The local time of a Slave Time Base will be maintained autonomously and updated
whenever a new time value is received from its associated Master Time Base.

7.3.4 Immediate Time Synchronization
All TSP Modules are working independently of the TS regarding the handling of the
bus-specific Time Synchronization protocol (i.e. autonomous transmission of Timesync
messages on the bus).
Time information is passed from a TSP to the TBR. Implementation details as well as
the interaction of such a TSP with the TBR are outside of the scope of this specifica-
tion(for protocol specification please refer to [1]).
7.3.5 User Data
User Data is part of each Time Base. User Data is set by the Global Time Master of
each Time Base and distributed as part of the Timesync messages.
User Data can be used to characterize the Time Base, e.g., regarding the quality of the
underlying clock source or regarding the progress of time.
User Data consists of a vector of bytes. Due to the frame format of various Timesync
messages it might not be possible to transmit the complete vector on every bus system.
It is the responsibility of the system designer to use only those User Data bytes in the
vector that can be distributed inside the vehicle network.
7.3.6 Time Correction
TS provides the ability for Time Slaves to perform Rate and Offset Correction of the
Synchronized TBR and Rate Correction of an Offset Time Base.
For Global Time Masters, the TS provides the ability to perform Rate Correction of their
Time Base(s).
Time correction can be configured individually for each Time Base.
7.3.6.1 Rate Correction for Time Slaves
Rate Correction detects and eliminates rate deviations of local instances of Time Bases
and of Offset Time Bases. Rate Correction determines the rate deviation in the scope
of a measurement. This rate deviation is used as correction factor which the TBR
uses to correct the Time Base's time whenever it is read (e.g. in the scope of
ara::
tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetCurrentTime
).

7.3.9 Global Time Validation Measurement Support
Figure 7.3 outlines the basic concept of the Time Validation feature.
A Time Slave collects information on the time synchronization process, to predict e.g.
the Sync Ingress based on its local instance of Global Time and check whether Master
and Slave agree upon the current time. The prediction itself will be locally analyzed
by a separate Adaptive Application to detect any existing impairments. Furthermore,
information on the time synchronization process from Time Masters and Slaves is also
shared with a Validator Adaptive Application which may run anywhere in the network,
e.g. on the owner of Global Time.
The Validator uses the information on the time synchronization process received from
the Time Master and Time Slave Entities via a user defined feedback channel to re-
construct the whole synchronization process and check that a coherent time base is
established among all peers.
The Time Validation feature only provides API to the Adaptive Application. The feed-
back channel and the actual validation performed by the respective Adaptive Applica-
tion is not standardized in AUTOSAR. It is done in a user defined way on application
level.

B Interfaces to other Functional Clusters (informative)
Note:
This is chapter is created in the scope of the new SWS document template and
in the current version is not applicable.
B.1 Overview
AUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between
Functional Clusters (on platform-level only), to allow efficient implementations, which
might depend e.g. on the used Operating System.
This chapter provides informative guidelines how the interaction between Functional
Clusters looks like, by clustering the relevant requirements of this document to describe
Inter-Functional Cluster (IFC) interfaces. In addition, the standardized public interfaces
which are accessible by user space applications (see chapters 8 can also be used for
interaction between Functional Clusters.
The goal is to provide a clear understanding of Functional Cluster boundaries and in-
teraction, without specifying syntactical details. This ensures compatibility between
documents specifying different Functional Clusters and supports parallel implementa-
tion of different Functional Clusters. Details of the interfaces are up to the platform
provider. Additional interfaces, parameters and return values can be added.
